judgment.rationale: Both are Class-1 Content bullets (rank 0, identical coordinate) under the same Competency C-1.10 ('Compare sequences and cycles of events and describe their duration using familiar units of time'). The first covers sequencing times of the day (morning, lunchtime, afternoon, night) and connecting them to familiar events and actions; the second ('Long and short time activities', LC: 'compare everyday activities to tell which takes a long time and which takes a short time') covers comparing event durations. These are complementary strands of the same early time competency — ordering/naming parts of the day versus qualitative duration comparison — with meaningful conceptual coherence around events and time, but the evidence shows no substantive extension, increase in complexity, or dependency in either direction at the same class rank, so no developmental direction is asserted. Shared ancestry, page proximity, and the single shared token 'time' alone would not justify an edge; the pair-specific coherence of familiar-event time reasoning supports symmetric relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-4.4 ('Develops strategies to estimate time') within CG-4 measurement. The Class-4 item is calendar-based duration computation ('Compute the number of days between the two given dates'; LC tags calculation/dates/days/time), while the Class-5 item is clock-time notation and conversion ('Normal time and railway time, 12 hour clock - 24 hour clock'; LCs distinguish normal vs railway time and convert 12-hour to 24-hour). These are complementary time-measurement sub-strands (calendar duration vs clock notation systems) rather than one extending or depending on the other: counting days between dates does not supply the notational conversion skill required for 12/24-hour clock work, so a Class-4-to-Class-5 buildsTowards is not substantively supported despite the one-rank gap. The shared 'time' LC tag and page/hierarchy proximity alone would not establish a relation, but the genuine same-competency coherence of estimating and working with time supports a symmetric relatesTo. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context; ancestors lack developmental coordinates and were used as context only.

That progression is pair-specific deepening rather than generic repetition, and earlier perceptual familiarity with symmetry plausibly supports success with rotation work. Evidence limitation: the Class-5 SFI text is a bare bullet ('Turns') and interpretation leans on its learning components; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry merge/audit context, which moderates confidence.
